summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against all ten paragraphs of the selected Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the refusals, warnings, purposes, speaker relationships, and difficult assertions without imposing additional doctrinal conditions. The simplified edition retains the substance independently of the standard. The bracketed wording is distinguished from manuscript punctuation, and the disclosed alternatives do not displace the working readings. Acceptance concerns fidelity to the supplied source and consistency with the attributed supplemental reports; it does not authenticate unseen editions, manuscript hands, photographs, or exhaustive collation.
